citation.sourceDocument: Arkansas DFA 2025 AR1000F Regular Income Tax Table + bracket-adjustment recapture; standard deduction; Ark. Code §26-51-201
citation.sourceNote: Arkansas levies a graduated tax (Ark. Code §26-51-201) on net taxable income = Arkansas AGI (≈ federal AGI for wage income) minus the standard deduction, with the SAME rate schedule for every filing status — Arkansas does not double the brackets for married couples (a married couple filing jointly, status 2, uses one schedule on combined income; the income-splitting status 4/5 that can keep more income in lower brackets is not modeled). The rates and thresholds come from ACT 2 of the 2026 First Extraordinary Session (approved 2026-05-06), amending Ark. Code §26-51-201(a)(4)(A) for tax years beginning on or after 2026-01-01: 0% on the first $5,599 of net taxable income, 2% to $11,199, 3% to $15,999, 3.4% to $26,399, and 3.7% above $26,400 — the top rate CUT from the 3.9% the 2025 AR1000F table prints. Read the act rather than the forms: the 2026 AR1000ES is stamped 10/2025, before the cut, and still prints 3.9%; the May-2026 withholding formula carries 3.70% and agrees with the act. The brackets reconcile to the dollar against Act 2's schedule (net taxable $61,000 → $1,889.80 = 2%·5,600 + 3%·4,800 + 3.4%·10,400 + 3.7%·34,600). DISTINCTIVE FEATURE — the BRACKET ADJUSTMENT (a high-income benefit recapture): for net taxable income above ~$94,700 Arkansas recaptures the benefit of its lower 0%/2%/3%/3.4% brackets, so a high earner's tax converges to a near-flat 3.9% schedule. This is modeled via the engine's new `incomeRecapture` capability: a flat amount that ramps linearly from $0 (at $94,700) to $287.30 (at $97,600) and stays there above. Act 2 narrowed the band and restated the adjustment as $290 falling $10 per $100 step; $287.30 is the exact gap between its two schedules above the band, which is what keeps the model exact there. The model is EXACT below the band (the graduated table) AND above it — at net taxable $100,000 Act 2's over-$94,700 schedule gives $3,620.10 (2% of the first $4,700 plus 3.7% of the rest), exactly the graduated $3,332.80 plus the $287.30 recapture, and every higher income matches it to the cent; only inside the narrow $94,700–$97,900 phase-in band does the engine's continuous ramp differ from the table's $100-step worksheet, by ≤ ~$15. The standard deduction is $2,470 (single / head of household / married-filing-separately / surviving spouse) or $4,940 (married jointly); married filing separately maps to single, and a qualifying surviving spouse to married jointly. OMITTED at launch fidelity, all the conservative (errs-high) direction except where noted: the Low Income Tax Tables (which zero out tax for AGI ≤ $14,643 single and reduce it up to ~$17,500 — so the engine over-taxes the lowest earners by ≤ ~$141, conservative), the $29-per-person personal tax credit (Form AR1000TC), the child-care and other AR credits, and Arkansas's indexing of the brackets/deduction for 2026 (the latest-published official 2025 schedule is used for the 2026 shard, the California/Vermont/Nebraska precedent — Arkansas held its 3.9% top rate, and the thresholds index ~2-3%/year so using the 2025 figures errs slightly high). Worked example, single $60,000 wages: net taxable = 60,000 − 2,470 = $57,530 (below the recapture band); tax = 2%·5,600 + 3%·4,800 + 3.4%·10,400 + 3.9%·(57,530 − 26,400) = 112 + 144 + 353.6 + 1,214.07 = $1,823.67. Verified against the official Arkansas DFA 2025 AR1000F Regular Income Tax Table and Ark. Code §26-51-201, and cross-checked against the Tax Foundation 2026 state-rate table on 2026-06-08.
